claim: The premise that the released Epstein documents show the people in them practicing Satanism does not survive a search of the release. Across the full extracted text of the Epstein Files Transparency Act production — all twelve Justice Department data sets plus the House Oversight estate holdings, 1,051,599 documents — "baphomet" appears in zero documents; "black mass" and "ritual sacrifice" in three each; "moloch" in seven; any form of "satanic/satanism/satanist" in 75. Read individually, those 75 fall into four groups: optical-character-recognition damage on scanned Deutsche Bank and UBS account statements, where the scanner renders "statement" and similar words as "satanist"; FBI open-source news summaries about the online extortion network known as 764 and the neo-Nazi group Order of Nine Angles, both of which post-date Epstein's death; book and manuscript passages in the estate holdings, including one that examines and rejects the Cathy O'Brien "Project Monarch" account and prints Michael Aquino's denial in full; and references to Salman Rushdie's "The Satanic Verses." No document in the release describes a ritual, a rite, or an occult practice by Epstein or anyone in his circle.

notes: Counts are document-level (one corpus line = one document) from ~/data/epstein-files/work/corpus.jsonl, run 2026-09-12: baphomet 0, moloch 7, black mass 3, ritual sacrifice 3, occult 154, lucifer 27, satani* 75. The 'occult' and 'lucifer' counts are not asserted in the claim because they were not individually read; satani* was, in full. The OCR failure mode is the same one documented in 2026-byington-claims-vs-corpus-001 — Deutsche Bank statement scans producing false hits. Aquino, a US Army PSYOP officer who founded the Temple of Set, was investigated in the Presidio day-care case and never charged; the estate manuscript is the only place his name appears in the release, and it appears there as a claim being refuted. This record answers the premise, not the metaphysics built on top of it.
